alex: heads-up — after the kernel-selection change landed yesterday, we see a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of user traffic. correlates with tokenizer bump + new batching heuristic.
maria: can you paste a quick repro or example keys?
alex: gist of one invalidated key: `{"prompt":"Hello\n\nCan you...","tool_call":{"name":"lookup_user","args":{"id":123}},"model":"redwood-1.2"}` — after tokenizer upgrade the same prompt tokenizes differently (extra token boundary) so the canonical key changed. also kernel route now sets `shape_hint` which changed batching behavior and timing for warmup.
jordan: ugh. so we have both tokenizer-version and an implicit kernel-routing factor affecting cacheability. i think we should treat tokenizer version as part of the cache fingerprint, not the whole prompt string.
sasha: agreed. two quick options: 1) include `tokenizer_version` in key meta (explicit) or 2) canonicalize to a stable normalized token-id signature we compute at encode time. option 2 means storing a small probe fingerprint in the key to avoid string diffs.
luis: option 2 sounds sturdier long-term but more invasive. downside: we'll have to maintain a stable encoder interface for fingerprints across runtime builds. we already have slight differences between byte-pair encoders in the infra images.
maria: for short-term, i propose: - pin tokenizer hash in the key (e.g. `tk_v:2025-03-01-commitabcdef`) - strip ephemeral tool metadata (timestamps, request_id) from `tool_call` fields before hashing - normalize JSON ordering and whitespace.

alex: i pushed a quick prototype that strips `tool_call.*.meta` and sorts object keys before hashing. running on canary now. early results: +6% hit-rate on canary, still shy of baseline for traffic where kernel routing changes timing.
jordan: kernel routing affects when KV warmup wins — some requests are now routed to fast-path kernels that don't get warmup prefetches because they arrive earlier in the batch lifecycle. Could explain remaining gap.
sasha: maybe we decouple warmup from kernel assignment: run the warmup probe at enqueue time, not after kernel is chosen. cost is more warmups but should raise hit-rate.
luis: real quick experiment plan: A) tokenizer-hash-in-key + normalize tool fields B) probe-fingerprint instead of raw prompt C) warmup-at-enqueue. run each for 24h against 5% traffic. we can measure hit-rate, extra tokens served (cost), and p50/p95 latency.
maria: + add metric: downstream reruns due to cache miss (how many callers immediately issue follow-ups). that's our user-visible impact.
ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout alex/cachekey-normalize v0.1 -> eng-runtime-canary (10%) by maria at 2025-06-12T14:12:03Z
alex: thanks. i'll attach the quick `normalize` snippet here for review:```python
# normalize prompt for cache key
import json

def normalize(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        out = {k: normalize(obj[k]) for k in sorted(obj.keys()) if k not in ("request_id","ts")}
        return out
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return [normalize(x) for x in obj]
    if isinstance(obj, str):
        return " ".join(obj.split())  # collapse whitespace
    return obj

# usage: key = sha256(json.dumps(normalize(payload), separators=(",",":"))).hexdigest()
```
maria: tiny nit — collapsing whitespace might change semantics for code blocks in prompts. maybe preserve triple-backtick sections by tokenizing and rejoining only outside code blocks.
jordan: good catch. also we should add `tokenizer_commit` header to the request so downstream services can log/compare.
sasha: i'll prototype the probe-fingerprint encoder today. it just emits a 64-bit fingerprint of the first N token ids normalized to tokeniser used. that should be stable and smaller than full token array.
luis: timeline: warmup change needs infra review (affects enqueue path). i'll put a ticket in eng-runtime backlog and try to get a safety review by EOD.
alex: action items: - maria: keep canary running and collect hit-rate + latency for 48h - sasha: probe-fingerprint POC by EOD - jordan: add tokenizer_commit header and logs - luis: infra PR for warmup-at-enqueue - all: decide whether tokenizer hash belongs in permanent key after POC.
maria: noted. i'll post canary metrics in this thread once we have 12h of data. :eyes:
luis: +1
